M03.intro: Organisation structure is where you describe your organisation in PeopleOS: the companies and legal entities that employ people, their registered establishments, your locations, and the business units, divisions, departments and teams people work in. Every employee's position points at these records, so you set them up first.
M03.why: Policies, approvals, data access, payroll and reports select people by company, location and department. If the structure is incomplete or wrong, rules miss people, payroll runs for the wrong employer and headcount reports do not add up.
M03.who: Tenant Super Admin can do everything here. Account Owner can create and change companies, legal entities, establishments and units and use the Organisation Designer. Tenant HR Admin manages companies, units, contacts and vendors but not legal entities or establishments. HR, payroll and attendance roles can view. Verifying a legal entity or establishment needs legal_entity.verify or establishment.verify (Tenant Super Admin by default).
M03.where: Organisation › Structure (Companies, Legal Entities, Establishments, Establishment assignments, Business Units, Divisions, Departments, Teams, Locations, Regions, Business Regions, Places, Cost Centres, Profit Centres, Dimension, Organisation contacts, Vendors, Organisation Designer) and Organisation › Org map. The same screens are listed under Admin › Setup › Core HR.
objectives: Set up companies, legal entities and establishments so each employee has the right employer and statutory place of work.
Create business units, departments, teams and locations and arrange them in the Organisation Designer.
Change, move or retire a unit safely, keeping the history, and read the Org map.
depends_on: M04 Masters and configuration: set the organisation name, industry and your own dimension name in Setup › Core HR first; apply a configuration pack before building masters.
M05 Users, access and integrations: an administrator whose data access is limited to some companies or locations sees only those units.
M07 Employees and the employee profile: the Org map and department headcounts need employees, positions and reporting lines.
M14 Statutory compliance and tax: PAN, TAN, PF, ESI, PT and other registrations are recorded against the legal entities and establishments made here.

procedures.title: Create a company
procedures.before: Decide the company's display name, a short code and its registered name. Set the organisation's industry in Setup › Core HR if new companies should default to it.
steps: Go to Organisation › Structure › Companies and click New company.
Enter Name (e.g. Demo Technologies), Code (DEMO-TECH), Legal name (Demo Technologies Pvt Ltd), keep Status Active, pick Industry. Click Next.
Optionally add Phone, Contact person, social links and a PNG or JPEG Logo. Click Next.
Check Country code (IN), and enter Timezone (Asia/Kolkata) and Currency (INR). Click Next.
Enter Effective from, for example the first day of the financial year; leave Effective to blank. Click Next.
Check the summary and click Create company.
Open Legal Entities and Establishments: a primary legal entity with the same code and an establishment coded MAIN now exist. Edit the establishment to set its State.
Open Organisation Designer, click Add root unit, choose Type Company, Place an existing unit, pick the company, add a reason and confirm.
procedures.result: The company is ready for locations, departments and hires, with its legal entity and principal establishment.

procedures.title: Register an establishment for another state and assign people to it
procedures.before: The legal entity exists. Have the registration certificate reference ready.
steps: Organisation › Structure › Establishments › New establishment. Choose the Legal entity, enter Code, Name and Establishment type.
Choose the Appropriate government for wages and for social security if you know them; Industry defaults from the company.
Enter Address, Country, State, District and Postal code. The State selects professional tax and labour welfare fund rules.
Keep Status Active, set Effective from, and save.
On the row, click Submit for verification and enter the certificate reference; attach a copy if you have one.
A second administrator with establishment.verify clicks Verify, checks the details and adds verification notes.
Open Establishment assignments › Assign establishment. Pick the Employee, Establishment, Effective from, Source and Reason, then confirm.
procedures.result: The establishment is verified and its employees have dated assignments, which statutory returns per establishment need.

procedures.title: Add a department and place it in the Designer
procedures.before: The company exists and is placed in the Designer. Create the cost centre first if the department should point to one.
steps: Choose Company, leave Parent department as None (a top-level department) or pick one, enter Name and Code, pick Cost centre, keep Status Active.
Enter Effective from if the department starts on a known date. Click Next.
Check Review and click Create department.
Organisation › Structure › Organisation Designer. Find the parent unit (company, business unit, location or department).
Hover the parent row and click the + (Add child). Choose Type Department and Place an existing unit.
Pick the department in Unit, enter a Reason for change and confirm. Unit added appears and the department shows under the parent.
procedures.result: The department exists and sits in the right place in the tree. Shortcut: in Add child choose Create a new unit to create and place it in one go.

procedures.title: Reorganise: move, rename or close a unit in the Designer
procedures.before: Agree the change with the business; know the date and the reason.
steps: Type its name or code in Search units by name or code.
Click Move, choose the New parent (only allowed parents are listed), enter a Reason for change and confirm.
Click Rename, enter the new Name and a reason. The new name shows everywhere, including past records.
Use Move up or Move down to change its order among units with the same parent.
Click Deactivate, enter the required reason and confirm: the unit and everything beneath it become Inactive.
Open the unit's edit page and its History tab to see the recorded change.
procedures.result: The tree reflects the new structure and each unit's History shows what changed and why.

warnings.title: Worked example: the Demo Group
warnings.headline: The example organisation has two companies, each with one legal entity and one principal establishment.
warnings.body: Use the example organisation to see how the pieces fit before you build your own. Names and numbers are fictional.
points: Companies: Demo Technologies (DEMO-TECH, Demo Technologies Pvt Ltd) and Demo Services (DEMO-SVC, Demo Services Pvt Ltd), both from 1 Apr 2025.
Legal entities: one primary per company, codes DEMO-TECH and DEMO-SVC, both Unverified.

Locations: Delhi (DEL) and Bangalore (BLR), offices of Demo Technologies.
Tree: Demo Technologies › Delhi › Facilities; Product (business unit) › Engineering (teams Platform, Mobile) and Design; Finance.
Demo Services › Consulting. About 20 people work in Demo Technologies and 2 in Demo Services.

warnings.title: Retire units; do not delete them
warnings.headline: Deleting a unit that any employee position uses fails, and deleting a company removes its legal entities and establishments.
warnings.body: Employee positions keep their history, so a unit used now or in the past must stay. Close it instead.
points: Set Status to Inactive and enter Effective to on the unit's edit page, or use Deactivate in the Designer.
Legal entities, establishments, vendors and establishment assignments cannot be deleted at all.
Regions, business regions and places with branches or places under them hide the Delete button.
warnings.todo: Use Delete only for a unit created by mistake that nobody uses.

warnings.title: Deactivation cascades; reactivation does not
warnings.headline: Deactivate in the Designer marks the unit and everything beneath it Inactive.
warnings.body: Reactivate restores only the unit you click. Sub-units stay Inactive until you reactivate each one.
points: A department cannot stay live inside an inactive division, so the cascade is deliberate.
A reason is required to deactivate and is kept in each unit's History.
warnings.todo: Before deactivating, check the units beneath; reactivate them one by one if you undo the change.

warnings.title: Verification needs a second person

warnings.body: Statutory returns check that the legal entity and establishment are Verified. Plan who submits and who verifies.

Editing an identity field of a verified record sets it back to Unverified.

M04.intro: Masters and configuration are the lists and settings the rest of PeopleOS chooses from: designations, grades, levels, employment types, categories, code series, document types, reasons, custom fields and forms, plus organisation-wide settings, feature flags, configuration packs and the Change Centre that governs changes.
M04.why: Hiring, policies, reports and approvals pick values from these lists. Missing or inconsistent masters mean incomplete employee records, policies that select the wrong people and codes that clash.
M04.who: Tenant Super Admin can do everything here. Tenant HR Admin manages people setup masters, custom fields, forms, document types, settings and packs, and can propose, publish and roll back configuration changes, but cannot approve them or switch feature flags. Account Owner manages people setup and settings and can view feature flags. Auditor has read-only access.
M04.where: Admin › All modules (Admin Centre), Admin › Setup (Setup centre, What do you want to configure?, Packs & blueprints, Change Centre, Custom fields, Forms, Designations, Grades, Levels, Job Families, Employment Types, Employee Categories, Work Modes, Employee code series, Number series, Document types, Qualifications, Option lists, Workforce reasons, Question banks, Feedback templates, Feature flags, Settings).
objectives: Find any configuration screen or setting from the Admin Centre, Setup or the configuration finder.
Set up job classifications, code series and reference lists in the right order, knowing what each one drives.
Apply a pack safely, use settings and feature flags knowingly, and govern changes through the Change Centre.
depends_on: M03 Organisation structure: companies must exist before per-company code series; departments before designations that name them.
M05 Users, access and integrations: roles decide who may change masters, settings and feature flags, and who approves changes.
M06 Workflows and policies: policies added by a pack, and their assignment rules, are managed there; rules select people by these masters.
M07 Employees and the employee profile: the hire wizard uses code series and every classification on the employee's position.

admin/change-centre--view.after: Approved changes publish at once, or on their effective date. Publishing writes the values to the record with CHANGE-number as the reference. Rollback is itself a change; nothing is deleted.
admin/change-centre--view.permission: configuration.approve to approve or reject; configuration.publish for Publish now; configuration.delete to discard; configuration.rollback to roll back.

procedures.title: Apply a configuration pack
procedures.before: Do this at the start, before you build levels, grades, job families and policies by hand. Note any settings you have already changed: the pack may overwrite them.
steps: Admin › Setup › Packs & blueprints. Read the description of each card under AVAILABLE PACKS.
Click Apply a pack, choose the Pack closest to your organisation (e.g. IT Company) and enter a Reason for change.
Confirm. The notification Pack applied lists how many records each section touched, e.g. levels: 6, policies: 4.
Open Levels, Grades and Job Families and rename or retire what you do not need.
Open the policies (M06) and their assignment rules: pack policies apply to Everyone until you change the rules.
The Enterprise pack also switches Configuration approval on: check Feature flags and Settings.
procedures.result: Your organisation starts from a sensible configuration that you then adjust. In the example organisation the levels, grades, job families and IT_LEAVE, IT_ATTENDANCE, IT_HOURS and IT_EXIT policies match the IT Company pack.

procedures.title: Add a designation
procedures.before: Create the level, grade, job family and department the designation should link to.
steps: Enter Name (e.g. Senior Software Engineer) and Code (SSE); choose Level (L4), Grade, Job family, Department; pick Employment types; keep Status Active.
Optionally enter the experience range, Minimum-wage skill category, Hazardous work and a Job description.
Leave blank, or enter the date the title starts.
Check Review and click Create designation.
procedures.result: The designation can be chosen when hiring and changing positions, and policy rules can select by it.

procedures.title: Configure the employee code series
procedures.before: Companies and employment types exist. Agree the code pattern for each company.
steps: Admin › Setup › Employee code series › New series.
Choose Company: All companies (default series) first, or a company. Leave Employment type blank unless the series is for one type.
Enter Prefix (e.g. DT-), Number of digits (4), Suffix (blank) and Next number (1).
Next code will be shows the first code, skipping codes already used (e.g. DT-0001).
Switch Allow typing a code by hand when hiring on or off.
Create the series; repeat for each company that needs its own pattern.
The NEXT CODE column shows what the next hire will get.
procedures.result: Each new hire gets the next code of their company's series automatically, with no clashes.

procedures.title: Add a custom field to employees
procedures.before: Agree the field's purpose, type and who may see it.
steps: Admin › Setup › Custom fields › New custom field.
Choose Entity Employee, enter Label (e.g. Laptop asset tag); check the suggested Key; choose Type; add Help text.
Set Required, Visible to employee, manager and HR, Employee may change it, Searchable and Reportable; keep Status Active.
Check Review and click Create custom field.
Open an employee's edit form: the field appears under Additional information.
procedures.result: The field is recorded on every employee and can be used in search and reports.

procedures.title: Switch on approval and approve a change
procedures.before: Agree who proposes and who approves. Approvers need configuration.approve (Tenant Super Admin by default).
steps: Admin › Setup › Feature flags › Edit on configuration.approval; turn Enabled on, give a reason, save.
Admin › Setup › Settings, search configuration.approval.minimum_risk, Edit and set low, medium or high.
Edit a governed record at or above the threshold (e.g. a company) and save: Submitted for approval appears.
Admin › Setup › Change Centre › Pending approval › View. Read WHAT CHANGES and IMPACT PREVIEW.
Click Approve (optional note) or Reject (note required). Approved changes publish at once.
On a published change click Roll back with a reason: a new change restores the old values.
procedures.result: Medium- and high-risk configuration edits are reviewed by a second person before they apply, with a full record.

calculations.title: How an employee code is made
calculations.intro: A code is the prefix, then the next free number padded with zeros to the number of digits, then the suffix. Figures are from the example organisation's Demo Technologies series.
explain: Prefix + number padded to Number of digits + Suffix. Numbers already taken in the pattern are skipped.
Company and type, then company, then type for all companies, then the default series.
Default employee code prefix + Digits: EMP and 5 in the example, last number 22, so EMP00023.
NEXT CODE column, Next code will be, and the hire wizard's Employee code step.

warnings.title: A pack overwrites, it does not merge
warnings.headline: Applying a pack or blueprint overwrites settings and every record with the same code; nothing is deleted.
warnings.body: Records are matched by code or key. A level L1 you renamed goes back to the pack's name, settings in the pack replace yours, and policies get a new version from today.
points: Pack policies come with an Everyone assignment rule: check rules in Workflows and policies (M06).
The Enterprise pack switches Configuration approval on and sets the minimum risk to medium.
Packs never create companies, departments, locations or designations.
Unless you are a Tenant Super Admin, importing a blueprint role can only grant permissions you hold.
warnings.todo: Apply a pack first, before your own edits, and export a blueprint beforehand if you have already configured things.

warnings.title: Settings and feature flags apply at once
warnings.headline: Changes on Settings and Feature flags take effect immediately and skip the Change Centre.
warnings.body: The Settings screen does not check values. A wrong type or a misspelt key can switch a behaviour off or do nothing.
points: Prefer the module's Setup page, which shows only settings PeopleOS reads and checks them.
Settings cannot be deleted; set the value back instead.
organisation.designer and security.mfa flags, and the locale.date_format, locale.time_format and branding.primary_colour settings, have no effect today.
warnings.todo: Always give a reason; the audit trail keeps before and after values.

warnings.title: Worked example: classifications in the Demo Group
warnings.headline: The example organisation uses six levels, six grades, seven job families and twelve designations.
warnings.body: Use it as a model of how the lists relate. Names are fictional.
points: Levels L1–L6 and grades G1–G6; job families Engineering, Quality, DevOps, Product management, Design, Human resources, Finance.
Designations include Software Engineer (L2), Senior Software Engineer (L4), Engineering Manager (L5) and Chief Executive Officer (L6).
Employment types: the seven defaults; employee categories: the eight defaults; work modes: Office, Remote, Hybrid, Field.
Code series: DT- (4 digits) for Demo Technologies, DS- (4 digits) for Demo Services; earlier codes run EMP00001 to EMP00022.
warnings.todo: Link each designation to a level at least, so reports and rules can group by seniority.

warnings.title: Deleting a custom field deletes its data
warnings.headline: Delete on a custom field removes every value stored in it, for every record.
warnings.body: Entity, Key and Type cannot be changed after saving, so plan them before creating the field.
points: To stop using a field, set Status Inactive or an Effective to date.
Hidden fields (visibility off) keep their values.

warnings.title: What the Change Centre does and does not govern
warnings.headline: Approval applies only to edits saved on edit pages, and only at or above the minimum risk.
warnings.body: With the configuration.approval flag off, edits apply at once and are not listed in the Change Centre; the record's History still shows them.
points: Low risk: designations, departments, teams, locations, levels, grades, job families, types, categories, work modes, regions, dimension values.
Medium risk: companies, business units, divisions, cost and profit centres, custom fields, forms, policies, salary components and structures.
Not governed: creating, deleting, Designer actions, Setup, Settings, Feature flags.
Edits from the edit pages carry no future date, so approved changes publish at once.
warnings.todo: Decide the minimum risk with your auditors and make sure at least two people can approve.
